questions.question: What distinguishes augmented reality from virtual reality in the type of experience it requires?
options: It is defined mainly by the user's psychological level of immersion.
It emphasizes augmenting real-world content with digital content instead of requiring immersion.
It requires a fully immersive experience by replacing the real environment.
It occupies the entire space between the real and virtual environment extremes.
questions.explanation: Augmented reality does not require an immersive experience and instead emphasizes adding digital content to real-world content.

questions.question: How can augmented reality be used in archaeology?
options: It can let a customer try cosmetic looks on a digital face before purchase.
It can scan a patient's vein network to support a medical treatment decision.
It can display things not visible to the naked eye and reconstruct lost structures.
It can measure room heights and lengths using a mobile phone.
questions.explanation: In archaeology, augmented reality can show things that are not visible to the naked eye and can reconstruct lost structures.

questions.question: How can augmented reality assist a worker in industrial manufacturing?
options: It can let a customer digitally paint walls on a screen before buying paint.
It can let a person see things while repairing or troubleshooting an industrial component.
It can place digital furniture in a scanned image of a customer's room.
It can trigger digital content when a device detects a QR code.
questions.explanation: In industrial manufacturing, augmented reality can allow a person to see things while repairing or troubleshooting a component of an industrial setup.

questions.question: Which augmented reality application area is a motivation for the metaverse concept?
options: Gaming, particularly well-known mobile augmented reality titles.
Archaeology, particularly reconstruction of lost structures.
Industrial manufacturing, particularly repair of industrial components.
Commerce, particularly e-commerce.
questions.explanation: The presence of many augmented reality applications in commerce, particularly e-commerce, is one motivation for the metaverse concept.

questions.question: How can an augmented reality passenger app help someone moving through a large airport terminal?
options: It can create a fully virtual terminal where the passenger can move before departure.
It can measure the heights and lengths of objects inside or outside the terminal.
It can show the passenger's exact location and the direction to take to reach a desired terminal.
It can let the passenger virtually try on luggage or accessories before buying them.
questions.explanation: The passenger app can use beacons at different points in the terminal to tell a passenger their exact location and the direction to move to reach a desired terminal.

questions.question: What can an augmented reality product-visualization app do before a customer buys a product?
options: It can let the customer digitally place or apply the product in a real-world view, such as furniture in a scanned room or paint on a wall.
It can let the customer measure the heights and lengths of objects inside or outside a room with a mobile phone.
It can let medical professionals interact with patients through telemedicine sessions.
It can let the customer virtually try cosmetic looks on a digital face or watch models on a digital hand.
questions.explanation: AR customer-experience product-visualization examples let a user scan a room and place IKEA objects in the digital image, or digitally paint walls on a screen, to see the effect before deciding whether to buy.

questions.question: What task can an augmented reality virtual tape measure application perform with a mobile phone?
options: It can tell a passenger their exact location and direction to a desired terminal.
It can visualize a patient's internal vein network by pointing at the skin surface.
It can measure the heights and lengths of objects inside or outside a room without a physical tape.
It can place digital watches on a customer's hand to compare models.
questions.explanation: The virtual tape measure application can measure the heights and lengths of objects inside or outside a room using a mobile phone, so a physical tape is not needed.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of an augmented reality virtual try-on application for retail?
options: It can let a customer preview cosmetic looks on a digital face or watch models on a digital hand before deciding to buy.
It can show a passenger the exact location and direction to a desired terminal.
It can let a customer preview furniture or wall paint in a digital view of their room before deciding to buy.
It can measure the heights and lengths of objects inside or outside a room with a mobile phone.
questions.explanation: Virtual try-on examples let customers try different cosmetic looks on a digital face or different watch models on a digital hand, and decide whether to buy based on look and feel.

questions.question: What can the handheld AccuVein device do in a healthcare setting?
options: It can measure the heights and lengths of objects inside or outside a room.
It can tell a passenger their exact location and direction to a desired terminal.
It can let a customer digitally paint walls on a screen before buying paint.
It can scan and visualize the patient's internal vein network to help decide a treatment course.
questions.explanation: AccuVein is a handheld AR device that scans a patient's vein network and, when pointed at the skin surface, allows the internal vein network to be visualized so the treatment course can be decided.

questions.question: What is the primary basis for categorizing augmented reality systems?
options: The technology used to develop and deploy them
The type of input hardware used
The position of the system on the reality-virtuality continuum
The level of immersion experienced by the user
questions.explanation: Augmented reality systems are categorized by the technology used rather than by psychological or immersive experience.

questions.question: Which four subcategories are used for markerless augmented reality applications?
options: Location-based, superimposition-based, projection-based, and immersive-based
Location-based, superimposition-based, projection-based, and marker-based
Location-based, superimposition-based, projection-based, and outlining-based
Location-based, superimposition-based, fiducial-based, and outlining-based
questions.explanation: Markerless augmented reality applications are divided into location-based, superimposition-based, projection-based, and outlining-based subcategories.

questions.question: In marker-based augmented reality, where does digital content appear after a marker is detected?
options: At the marker's position in the real-world view
On a surface selected by a light projector
At the center of the device's display
At the user's current GPS location
questions.explanation: When a marker-based AR device detects a placed marker, the desired digital content appears at that marker's position in the real-world view.

questions.question: What do markerless augmented reality applications allow that marker-based applications do not?
options: Users to receive content only at a GPS location
Users to view graphics projected onto a surface by a light projector
Users to place virtual objects without physical markers
Users to trigger content by scanning a fiducial marker
questions.explanation: Markerless AR does not require physical markers and allows users to decide where to place virtual objects, while marker-based AR relies on markers to trigger content.

questions.question: Which markerless augmented reality subtype uses light projectors to place digital content on an object, surface, or space?
options: Projection-based augmented reality
Superimposition-based augmented reality
Outlining-based augmented reality
Location-based augmented reality
questions.explanation: Projection-based markerless AR uses light projectors to project digital graphics, characters, or other content onto an object, surface, or space.

questions.question: What do virtual reality system categories primarily distinguish?
options: The display hardware used by the system
The user's experience or psychological aspect
The application domain of the system
The technology used to develop and deploy the system
questions.explanation: VR system categories are based on the experience or psychological aspect, comprising non-immersive, semi-immersive, and fully immersive systems.

questions.question: What do augmented reality system categories primarily distinguish?
options: The technology used to develop and deploy the systems
The user's psychological or immersive experience
The type of immersive display used
The application domain of the systems
questions.explanation: AR system categories are based primarily on the technology used to develop and deploy the systems rather than on the psychological aspect.

questions.question: Why are markerless augmented reality techniques used to address a limitation of marker-based systems?
options: Markers are difficult to maintain unless the environment is very sanitized
Markers depend on GPS sensors for placement
Markers prevent digital content from appearing in the real-world view
Markers require complex computer-vision algorithms
questions.explanation: Marker-based AR systems are easier to make because they rely on simple algorithms, but their markers are hard to maintain unless the environment is very sanitized. Markerless techniques are used to overcome this maintenance difficulty.

questions.question: What do markerless augmented reality techniques rely on primarily?
options: Computer vision, with other sensors such as GPS in location-based applications
Physical markers, such as QR codes and fiducial markers
Fully immersive virtual environments without a real-world view
Psychological immersion levels, such as semi-immersive experience
questions.explanation: Markerless AR techniques rely primarily on computer vision and may rely on other sensors, such as GPS sensors, in location-based applications.

questions.question: What is the main difference in how VR and AR applications are characterized?
options: AR applications are categorized by psychological immersion, whereas VR applications are categorized by display technology
VR applications are immersive, whereas AR applications emphasize augmenting digital content onto the real-world view
VR and AR have completely different application domains
VR applications rely on markers, whereas AR applications rely on GPS sensors
questions.explanation: VR and AR have broadly similar application domains. VR applications are characterized as immersive, while AR applications emphasize augmenting digital content onto the real-world view rather than being immersive applications.

questions.question: How does augmented reality differ from virtual reality in the kind of experience it aims to provide to the user?
questions.reference_answer: Augmented reality does not require an immersive experience and instead emphasizes augmenting real-world content with digital content. Virtual reality applications are characterized as immersive, and an immersive experience is one perceived through the senses as real rather than distinguishable from the user's real environment. Thus augmented reality adds digital content to the real-world view, whereas virtual reality applications aim to provide an immersive experience.

questions.question: Why can markerless augmented reality techniques be useful for augmented reality systems that would otherwise rely on physical markers?
questions.reference_answer: Marker-based augmented reality systems use markers placed in the environment, and those markers are prone to damage, making the systems difficult to maintain unless the environment is very sanitized. A damaged marker may make the application not work, especially in outdoor or less well-attended settings. Markerless augmented reality techniques overcome this maintenance difficulty by not requiring physical markers and by relying primarily on computer vision or other sensors such as GPS.

questions.question: How do augmented reality applications in commerce and retail connect to the metaverse idea in extended reality?
questions.reference_answer: Extended reality technologies have application potential in domains such as retail, and augmented reality has applications in commerce, particularly e-commerce. The presence of many augmented reality applications in commerce, particularly e-commerce, is one motivation for the metaverse concept. The metaverse has heavily stimulated growth in the extended reality field, so these commerce-oriented augmented reality applications help show why the metaverse idea became relevant.

questions.question: How do location-based and superimposition-based markerless augmented reality applications use different sensor or recognition methods to add digital content to the real world?
questions.reference_answer: Markerless augmented reality techniques can rely primarily on computer vision, and they may also rely on sensors such as GPS in location-based applications. Location-based markerless augmented reality applications rely on a location sensor such as GPS to detect the user's location with respect to a reference frame and augment digital content when the user is at a specific location. Superimposition-based markerless augmented reality applications recognize one or multiple physical objects using computer vision techniques and superimpose digital content on the real-world scene depending on the recognized objects.
